memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.” – Luke 8:8

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
In these days, people do not refuse to hear; rather, they refuse to hear truly. They want to hear only what they like, what is comfortable, and what fits their lifestyle. Words of correction, repentance, and inner conviction are often avoided. Jesus did not say, “He who has ears, let him hear,” but “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

Many people heard Jesus preach, but only a few listened attentively. Some listened without interest, some with carelessness, and others only to find fault. The Pharisees listened in order to accuse, the crowds listened for entertainment, but the disciples listened for inner transformation. What a difference! Hearing without the fear of God produces pride, but hearing with the fear of God produces obedience.

True listening always walks hand in hand with godly fear. Words heard without the fear of God remain mere information; words received with reverence become revelation. The same Word softens a humble heart but hardens a careless one. The problem is not with the seed of the Word, but with the ears that hear and the heart that receives.
People are not blessed merely because they hear much, but because they listen carefully and practice what they hear with godly fear. God is still speaking, but only those who fear Him truly listen. Our ears should not be collectors of sermons, but instruments of transformation that lead to obedient action.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “The Word of God does not change those who do not tremble at it.”- A. W. Tozer

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, grant us ears that truly hear and hearts that tremble at Your Word. Remove carelessness and pride from us, and produce obedience within us. O Lord, sharpen our ability to listen and bring our lives under submission to Your truth.
In Jesus’ Name, Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: “Your spiritual life is not measured by how much you hear, but by how much you surrender yourself to be transformed.”
